sfk_annotated_page.description: The page came off a Moonwalker, and Arugal didn't write it. It's a survey of a keep, drawn in a neat court hand, with the inner ward measured and the garrison strength noted in the margin. The keep isn't Shadowfang. Somebody in Alterac is paying for surveys of somebody else's walls, and somebody in Shadowfang was carrying one.
sfk_annotated_page.accept_text: The hand is a court hand, and the subject is a keep in Hillsbrad. There's a Forsaken scholar watching that keep from the bluff above it who'll know exactly what she's looking at.
sfk_annotated_page.turn_in_text:
Where did you get this, Shadowfang? A worgen was carrying this?

This is Durnholde, measured, inner ward and all, in an Alterac hand. They've been surveying their own keep for someone else, or someone else has been surveying it for them, and I don't know which answer I like less.

Stay in this valley. There's work here now, and you've just made some of it.

spn_wl_brood.description:
My name's Yseult. I carve what the tombs give up, and lately what the Widow's Lair gives up.

Corvane the webhunter has been inside the mouth of the Lair, not far, but far enough to count, and counting is his job. He says there are hatchlings in the thousands. He's said that figure to three officers and watched all three decide he was exaggerating. He wasn't exaggerating. He counted a section and multiplied.

And there are silk-bound weavers tending them, which should worry people more than the number. Something in the Lair is being looked after.

Thin the first rooms before anyone tries the deeper ones. Take the hatchlings first. The weavers sit above them and spit, and you won't see the first one coming.
spn_wl_brood.accept_text: They're inside the Lair, around the Web Heart.
spn_wl_brood.turn_in_text:
That's fewer legs.

That's the best thing I can say about that place right now, and I've been trying to think of a second one for a week.

spn_wl_journal.description:
It's a silk-wrapped page, pulled off a Brood Warden's carapace, and it's been in there a while.

It's a hunter's hand, small, cramped, written fast, by somebody writing in a bad light who expected to be reading it back later. The last entry begins:

I've counted the exits, and there are only two.

There's nothing after that line. The page isn't torn. It simply stops, and the ink on the last word is heavier than the rest, as though the pen stayed where it was for a while. The silk around it was spun afterward, deliberately and tightly, the way the weavers wrap anything they intend to keep.

The Apothecary at the Rear Guard keeps a list of the missing. He's kept it for eleven years, and he keeps it properly.
spn_wl_journal.turn_in_text:
That's Marek Dunn.

I had him down as lost to wolves. I've had him down as that for two years, and I wrote it myself.

A spider is worse, and better too. He was somebody doing his job, right up to the last line of it.

I'll correct the list.

spn_wl_silka.description:
The hive buds off a single queen, and her name is Silka. She's in the west lair, off the Web Heart.

Here's what that means, and it's why I'm sending you at her rather than at the numbers. Everything Longleg ever was came out of her eggs. Every spider in those woods that anybody has ever lost a dog or a child to comes from one line, from one source, and the source is still laying.

Corvane assumed for years that the woods simply had spiders, the way woods do. Then he counted, and his count only works if there's one.

End the line. Follow the egg sacs west. They get thicker the closer you are. She's what they're all running from, and Corvane's watched them do it.
spn_wl_silka.accept_text: Go into the Widow's Lair. Take the west lair off the Web Heart, and follow the egg sacs.
spn_wl_silka.turn_in_text:
There'll be no more eggs.

For the first time since the plague, these woods will have fewer legs in them next year than this one.

Thank you. I've waited a long while to be able to say a sentence like that.

spn_wl_skitter.description:
There's a second queen-brood in the east lair, under a weaver called Skitter. Don't go in with the same plan you used on Silka.

Silka lays, and that's all she does. She's a source, and the hive flows away from her. Skitter keeps what she catches. She hangs her victims from the ceiling for later, alive, some of them, for considerably longer than you'd think possible. Corvane has been close enough to that lair to establish it, and he wishes he hadn't.

He's watched it from the mouth for a season, and he'd like to stop watching it, and I'd like him to. That's the honest whole of my reason, and it isn't strategic.

She's east of the Web Heart. And look up before you step in, not after.
spn_wl_skitter.turn_in_text:
They were hung up like laundry, the whole east lair.

Well, not any more.

spn_wl_velaxis.description:
Above the Web Heart there's a spire, and Velaxis nests in it.

She's older than Silka and larger than Skitter, and she isn't fond of company, which in anything else I'd call a personality and in her I'd call a warning.

She's the head of this hive. Silka was the source and Skitter was the keeper, and both of them answered upward. Corvane didn't believe spiders did that until he spent a season at the mouth of that place watching them. Cut her off, and the hive is a lot of legs with nothing arranging them.

Go up the north neck from the Web Heart. The Spire is lit by her eyes, and that's how you'll know you've arrived. I won't pretend this is anything but a death sentence for whoever tries it. Corvane has watched two go up that neck.
spn_wl_velaxis.accept_text: Go into the Widow's Lair, up the north neck from the Web Heart, into the Matriarch's Spire.
spn_wl_velaxis.turn_in_text:
All eight eyes are closed.

I'll rest easy tonight, and so will these woods, and I'll tell Corvane he can finally put that word in a report.

You've earned every copper, and a good deal more I haven't got.

spn_wl_venom.description:
I'm Apothecary Pell. Don't lean over the cauldron. It's at a delicate stage, and so am I.

My venom theory has acquired a new requirement, which is what theories do when they're going well. I need stalker venom. The Silverpine spider glands I've been using aren't strong enough, by a good half, which I established the tedious way over four months and eleven batches.

The Venom Stalkers inside the Lair have what I want. Cut the sac at the base, seal it, and then run, in that order, because two of my suppliers reversed the last two.

And please don't open one to look. Everybody wants to look. It's green, it's famous, and the one who looked is why I now say this to everybody.
spn_wl_venom.accept_text: Take them off the venom stalkers inside the Widow's Lair, and seal them.
spn_wl_venom.turn_in_text:
Oh, that's beautiful, thick as syrup and green as a corpse.

The Dark Lady's Apothecaries will want to hear about this, and for once I'll be the one telling them.

sps_at_atiesh.description:
The tower's last occupant is Archmage Atiesh, and he keeps the Observatory, which is where the waygate was aimed.

Nobody at Ambermill has put those two facts side by side, and the moment you do, the whole building reorganises itself around them. That's an observatory with a tower under it, and everything beneath, the reading hall, the lab, the lecterns, Hawren, was support. Somebody was looking at something for a very long time, and the waygate was how the looking got out.

I want to know what he was aiming at. And I'll say this plainly: I hope the answer dies with him.

Go to the very top. The stair is long. Don't stop on the landings, not to rest and not to look. The landings are where it talks to you.
sps_at_atiesh.turn_in_text:
He aimed it at the stars.

It was just the stars, a man looking up, for decades, carefully.

And then the stars aimed back.

Thank you. I'll be some time with that.

sps_at_hawren.description:
Orsolo is a long time getting to it, and when he does he's very matter-of-fact.

Magister Hawren keeps the Archivist's Gallery. He was my teacher. He taught me to read, and then to read carefully, and then that the second one is a different skill.

He no longer remembers a pupil's name. I stood in the vestibule eleven days ago and said my own name up that stair, twice, and the gallery didn't change. So there's nothing to be recovered, and I've stopped looking for a version where there is.

The Archivist's Gallery is west of the reading hall, and he's surrounded by his own pages. I can't do it myself. I'd like that on the record as cowardice rather than protocol, because that's what it is.
sps_at_hawren.turn_in_text:
He'd want to be remembered for something better.

I'll try to oblige. I've got all his pages now, and that's more of him than most teachers leave.

sps_at_ledger.description:
It's a ledger, pulled out of an alchemist's coat. The cover is stained through with something that was once a flask.

It's kept properly, by somebody who was never going to be audited and did it correctly anyway.

And it's page after page of orders for reagents of discretion. It's that exact phrase, every time, for years, with never a description, never a quantity in plain words, never a name for what was in the crate.

Every single order is initialled with the same letter, H, in the same careful hand, down the whole right-hand margin.

The millwright at the mill has been buying from the same valley his whole working life. He'll know the initial, and he'll know it immediately.
sps_at_ledger.turn_in_text:
H is for Helbrim.

He sold the mill its lamp-oil for eleven years. He came by in person and asked after my apprentices by name.

I'd have said he was a decent man, and I'd have said it in front of anybody. I won't any more.

sps_at_mages.description:
The reading hall is staffed by the dead, and I use the word staffed deliberately. They're Kirin Tor and Forsaken mages who kept studying after they stopped breathing.

A haunting repeats. These are working, moving between lecterns, taking things down, putting things back. What finally convinced me was that the stacks are in order. Somebody is shelving.

And there are imps bound to the lecterns, which tells you a living hand did the binding at some point, because an imp doesn't stay on a lectern out of professional interest.

I want the hall cleared so I can walk it. The mages cast first, all of them, immediately, and they don't posture about it. The imps hold the doors, so expect to fight your way back out as well as in.
sps_at_mages.turn_in_text:
I can walk it now.

Perhaps even a very brave librarian could, and I know two.

sps_at_orrery.description:
One last thing, and then the magister locks the door.

The Orrery is the Observatory's twin, east of it, a round room full of little worlds, all still turning. Nobody has wound anything in that building for decades, and those worlds are keeping time. That's what the waygate has been feeding.

And here's the thing I've worked out and can't explain. They go out when somebody stands in the room, a living person, present, for about a minute. Then the lamps settle and the little worlds slow, and when you leave they don't start again.

I don't know what that means. I know I want it done. Go to the Observatory first, then the Orrery to the east, and just be there for a minute in each.
sps_at_orrery.turn_in_text:
They're both dark now.

The waygate sleeps.

Orsolo will lock it and give me the key, and I'll keep it somewhere stupid and not tell you where, because then three of us would know.

sps_at_reagents.description:
The Alchemy Lab was Dalaran's best-stocked apothecary outside the Violet Citadel. That's an enormous amount of material in one room, sealed and sitting there.

And its alchemists never stopped brewing. They've done it for decades, in a sealed room, with no one taking anything out. I'm a millwright, and even I can see where that ends. Every batch they finish has to go somewhere, and it's been going into the floor, and the floor is above the lower hall.

I want sealed vials out of there before the slow poison gets properly out of hand. I want enough for somebody to say what's in the floor.

The Forsaken Alchemists carry them on their belts, north-east of the lower hall. Follow the smell, and don't breathe it.
sps_at_reagents.turn_in_text:
They're sealed, thank the Light, and not yet leaking.

I'll have them neutralised by dawn, and I won't sleep until they are.

sps_at_vestibule.description:
I'm Tamsin Hale, and I scribe for Magister Orsolo, and with Quillfire silent he can finally say this out loud without somebody shouting it down. That waygate was keeping something.

Everybody has treated it as a door nobody uses. A door nobody uses gets left alone, and this one has been maintained. You can see the difference from the outside if you know what a maintained ward looks like. So something on the other side was worth the upkeep, and somebody was paying it until very recently.

The tower's lowest rooms are a vestibule and a reading hall above it. Stand in both and tell me whether the lamps are still lit. Those lamps don't burn oil. If they're lit, something is still putting power into that building, and if they're violet, it's listening.
sps_at_vestibule.accept_text: Step into the waygate, and go to the vestibule first, then the reading hall up the stair.
sps_at_vestibule.turn_in_text:
They're still lit, and violet.

So it's listening.

Thank you, truly. The magister's been arguing for permission to ask that question for two years, and I've been writing the letters.

sps_sfk_arugal.description:
Archmage Arugal opened the door that let the worgen into Lordaeron.

Everybody knows that sentence, and almost nobody follows it through. He opened a door, as a measure against the Scourge, and it worked, briefly, and then it kept being open. Everything in this valley since has come out of it: the hills, the keep, Pyrewood, Rynn's whole trade. And he sits at the top of this keep with his tower of shadow, and he seems to think it went well.

I've stood at his gate nineteen years. I'd like to see the other side of it.

Go to the upper landing, then the Sanctum. Don't stop, and don't answer when he speaks. He will, and it'll sound like a question you'd want to answer.
sps_sfk_arugal.accept_text: Go to Shadowfang Keep, to the upper landing, then Arugal's Sanctum at the top of the keep.
sps_sfk_arugal.turn_in_text:
So Arugal's dead.

I'll lock the gate and sit for a while. I'm going to sit for a long while.

Thank you. You'll never need to buy a drink at the March, and I'll be back at my gate tomorrow, because I don't know how not to be.

sps_sfk_bailey.description:
I'm Marl, the gatekeeper, which out here means I stand at a gate nobody goes through and nobody comes out of, and I've done it for nineteen years.

In all that time I've never once met a person who could tell me what the forecourt looks like. People come out of Shadowfang, not many, but some, and I've spoken to every one of them. They'll tell you about the Great Hall. They'll tell you about the kennels at length. Not one of them has ever described the bailey. I've stopped thinking that's a coincidence.

So go through the portcullis, down the gatehouse passage, out into the bailey, and stand by the fountain. It's dry, I know that much from the gate. Then come back and tell me, while it's fresh.
sps_sfk_bailey.turn_in_text:
It's a dry fountain and a lot of bones.

I'd imagined worse. Nineteen years of imagining, and it's bones.

You've got the nerve to go further. I'd like to make use of that.

sps_sfk_cloister.description:
West of the Great Hall there's a stone cloister that runs out to Fenrus' crypt.

Nobody has walked it in years. I want to be careful there. People have survived it. They just don't walk it. Everyone who gets that far turns and takes the armoury stair instead, and when I ask them why, they can't tell me.

I'd like it walked, start to end, and I'd like one specific thing from it. I need to know whether the crypt door is open.

If it's shut, then whatever's in there has been shut in since Arugal's day, and the keep has been containing it. If it's open, then it's been open for years, and everything in that building has been living alongside it on purpose.

Go out of the west door of the Great Hall, down the cloister, into the crypt, and just look.
sps_sfk_cloister.turn_in_text:
So it's open.

I'd hoped for that and feared it, both, honestly, and I couldn't have told you which was stronger until you said it.

sps_sfk_fenrus.description:
Fenrus was Arugal's first experiment and his least successful. I've had that from two sources, and neither of them was being kind about it. Least successful means it didn't do what he wanted. It's very much alive down there.

He devours things in the crypt, and nothing that goes in comes out. That's a tally, not drama. Marl's kept the gate nineteen years, and he knows what's gone down that cloister and what hasn't come back up it, and the two numbers are the same number.

Marl and I would like, once, for something to come back out of that hole on its own feet.

He's at the end of the cloister. And mind the sarcophagi on the way down. Three people have told me they breathe, and I've stopped asking them to explain it.
sps_sfk_fenrus.turn_in_text:
He ate his handler, and then his handler's replacement.

That's what least successful meant, and I've been chewing on it since you went down.

Thank you for being the exception.

sps_sfk_guards.description:
I'm Ashe, the field surgeon. I take things apart for a living, and Shadowfang has a few I'd like taken apart.

The keep's old guard never left their posts. The guardsmen wail where they were posted, which I know because the positions make sense. Stand in the Great Hall and you can read the old watch order off them. And the officers keep giving orders, to no one, out loud, in the proper form, with pauses where the acknowledgement should go.

They were never relieved. Somebody should have come to take that watch, and nobody ever did, and they're all still standing there waiting for it.

So relieve them, one way or another. Take the officers first, then the men. That's the order it should have happened in, and it's the only courtesy left to pay them.
sps_sfk_guards.accept_text: Go to Shadowfang Keep, south of here, the Great Hall and the passages around it. Take the officers first.
sps_sfk_guards.turn_in_text:
They're all relieved now.

It's a kindness, and I'm glad it wasn't me who had to do it, and I'm ashamed of being glad.

sps_sfk_keys.description:
Here's a practical one, and it'll make everything after it cheaper.

The haunted servitors still carry the keep's keys on their belts, a full ring each. They aren't guarding the doors. They're simply still carrying what they carried, because that's what a servitor does and nobody ever took them back.

Right now the cloisters and the armoury are a gamble. You come to a door in that keep, you don't know if it's locked, and you find out by standing in front of it long enough for something to arrive. I've stitched up what that costs.

Look in the Great Hall and the cloisters. Take the ring, not the key. I want whole rings, because a ring tells you which doors went together, and that's a floor plan, and nobody's ever had one of those.
sps_sfk_keys.accept_text: Take them off the haunted servitors in the Great Hall and cloisters of Shadowfang Keep. I want whole rings.
sps_sfk_keys.turn_in_text:
They're the right doors, and none of them haunted.

That's almost enough to make a person hopeful.

sps_sfk_razorclaw.description:
My name's Pell. Marl keeps the Shadowfang gate, and I take his nights.

The Butcher's Yard is east of the bailey, and Razorclaw keeps it. He's a worgen with a cleaver where a hand ought to be. He doesn't hold one, he has one instead, and two people who got too close have confirmed it.

Marl's heard the chopping from this gate for years, and I've heard it every night watch since I got here. It's regular, and it isn't a frenzy or a fight. It's the sound of a man working, at a steady pace, for hours, and then stopping, and then starting again the next day. Something is being prepared in that yard on a schedule, and the schedule hasn't changed in all the time Marl's stood at that gate.

Follow the sound. You'll hear it from the gatehouse.
sps_sfk_razorclaw.accept_text: Go to Shadowfang Keep. The Butcher's Yard is east of the bailey. Follow the sound.
sps_sfk_razorclaw.turn_in_text:
The chopping's stopped, thank the Light.

I'll sleep tonight, for the first time in a long while, and I'll probably wake up listening for it.

sps_sfk_silverlaine.description:
Baron Silverlaine owned Pyrewood, and Shadowfang, and half the pines between. Most of the people who worked them never saw him.

He sits on his dais in the Great Hall and receives no one, and that's exactly what he did alive. Nothing about his conduct has changed. He held court and received nobody, and he does the same now. The only difference is that now there's genuinely nobody to receive.

I'd prefer the hall empty. I don't want him avenged or reckoned with. As long as he's sitting at the far end of it, that keep still has an owner, and a keep with an owner is a place other things come to serve in.

He's at the far end of the Great Hall. He doesn't stand. He doesn't need to, and he never has.
sps_sfk_silverlaine.accept_text: Go to Shadowfang Keep. He's at the far end of the Great Hall, on the dais.
sps_sfk_silverlaine.turn_in_text:
That's a fitting end, I suppose.

He'd have called it a very modest funeral, and he'd have meant it as a complaint.

sps_sfk_sons.description:
The inner keep is stocked with Arugal's best, and I use stocked with intent. There are Sons of Arugal in half-turned shapes, and Lupine Horrors that don't fit through the doors they're standing behind. And there are Deathsworn Captains, who command them.

That last part is why I won't call this a pack. A pack sorts itself out. It has a top and a bottom, and every animal in it knows where it stands without anybody writing it down. This has officers. Something decided who commands whom, and that's a cult with fangs, and a cult doesn't break when you kill the biggest one.

Clear the crypt, the armoury and the upper landing. Don't fight them in a corridor. That's where the Horrors are useful, and they know it.
sps_sfk_sons.accept_text: Go back into Shadowfang Keep, south-west of here. Clear the crypt, the armoury and the upper landing, and don't fight in a corridor.
sps_sfk_sons.turn_in_text:
It's a cult with fangs, like I said.

Fewer of those is a victory, and I'll take it as one. I'd still rather be fighting wolves.
